2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.

With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

description: "macOS crash when a wxWebView is destroyed while Orca's deferred AddScriptMessageHandler waits in a nested wxYield; a frame's Destroy() is deferred to idle, so also delete the view synchronously"
metadata:

Found 2026-09-18 (printer-setup shell harness exit 139 after PASS, at 0e55c4f9be).

Orca's `WebView::CreateWebView` (src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp) installs each view's "wx" message handler from a `CallAfter`. On macOS wx's `AddScriptMessageHandler` then runs a *synchronous* `RunScript`, which spins `wxYield` until WebKit answers, with `GUI_App::is_adding_script_handler()` true. Any pending CallAfter can run inside that yield. If it destroys that web view, WebKit later cancels the reply and calls `SendScriptResult` on the freed view → segfault in `wxEvtHandler::SafelyProcessEvent`. The JusPrin bridge's own sends are NOT the cause: `WebView::RunScript` on Mac uses `WKWebView_evaluateJavaScript` with no completion.

**Why:** a panel opened and closed within one event-loop turn (harness, or fast clicks) tears down before the install finishes.

**How to apply:** never delete a web view (or its owner) while `is_adding_script_handler()` is true. Hide it, cut its callbacks, and retry on a timer, as `PrinterPanel::tear_down_runtime` does (branch claude/printer-panel-exit-crash) and as `GUI_App::run_wizard` already did. Any other short-lived AgentWebView owner needs the same guard. Related: [[workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac]], [[agent-setup-embedded-in-printer-dialog]].

SECOND VARIANT (2026-09-29, `--printer-setup` exit 139 after `host_attempt_starts_waiting`): Home's `PrinterWindow` (a top-level frame holding Orca's `PrinterWebView`) was closed with `Destroy()` right after opening. A top-level frame's `Destroy()` only queues deletion for the next idle; the view's queued install then ran, and that idle came *inside* the install's nested yield. So checking `is_adding_script_handler()` when closing is not enough: the install had not started yet. Fix (branch claude/printer-setup-harness-crash): `PrinterWindow::close()` deletes the page view synchronously (a child's `Destroy()` is immediate, and `~wxEvtHandler` drops its queued CallAfter install), only when the flag is false; otherwise hide and retry on a 50 ms timer. Found by lldb breakpoints on `wxWebViewWebKit::~wxWebViewWebKit` and `RunScriptAsync` (print `$x0`, `bt 80`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the clang-tidy check that gates pull requests (.github/workflows/clang_tidy.yml)
# on your branch, so its findings match what CI reports. Linux and macOS.
#
#   scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh            check your changes against OrcaSlicer's main
#   scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh --fix      also add the missing includes it names
#
# It configures a separate build directory (build-tidy) without the precompiled
# header, uses the clang-tidy on your system or installs the pinned one into a
# virtual environment inside it, and runs scripts/clang_tidy_diff.py the way CI
# does. Uncommitted changes are checked too.
set -euo pipefail
usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh [options]
  -b, --base REV       revision to compare against (default: main of the remote that
                       points at OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer, else origin/main)
      --no-fetch       do not fetch that remote's main first
  -B, --build-dir DIR  build directory for the compile database (default: build-tidy)
  -d, --deps-dir DIR   dependency build directory (default: deps/build on Linux,
                       deps/build/<arch> on macOS)
  -j, --jobs N         parallel clang-tidy runs (default: all cores)
      --fix            apply clang-tidy's fixes (adds the missing includes)
  -y, --yes            install missing tools without asking; another clang-tidy
                       version found on the system is then not offered
  -h, --help           show this help
EOF
}
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
cd "$ROOT"
BASE=""
FETCH=1
BUILD_DIR=build-tidy
DEPS_DIR=""
JOBS=""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run clang-tidy on the C++ files changed since a base revision.
Check findings are reported only on added or modified lines, so existing code
is not held to checks it predates. A changed source file that does not compile
(for example one that only built because the precompiled header supplied an
include) fails wherever the error is. Headers are compiled on their own, and
fail only on errors in their changed lines. Deleting an #include also fails
on every use, changed or not, that now lacks the header it provided.
With -- --fix, clang-tidy adds the missing includes, on those lines only, and
each file it changed is checked again so that only what remains is reported.
The checks come from .clang-tidy at the repository root. The compile database
must come from a configure with SLIC3R_PCH=OFF, or the precompiled header hides
missing includes.
    python3 scripts/clang_tidy_diff.py -p build-tidy --base origin/main

- "Choose **Plate settings…**." ends in "…." because the menu name carries the ellipsis. Same with "Version history…." elsewhere.
- "In the **Plates** tab at the left": the picture next to it shows the Plates tab, but in the app the left pane starts collapsed and shows only a strip reading "Objects · 1", so a reader looking for a "Plates tab" does not find it.
- The plate picture shows Plate 2 with no menu open, so it does not show the step it sits under ("open the plate's "···" menu").
- "The window holds what can differ per plate" names no window; the reader did not know which window opened.
- Jargon a newcomer did not know: presets, print sequence, spiral vase, "once AI is set up".
- In the dark window the pictures stay light (they are light-mode captures). Readable, but they look pasted in. Dark captures would need run_guide_checks.py to take each picture twice.

Help › JusPrin guide…: a window that searches the app guide and shows its pages

The Help menu gains "JusPrin guide…" above Ask AI…. It opens a window over
the app, not modal, 960 × 680: the guide's pages at the left in the order
docs/guide/README.md lists them, the open page's sections under its title,
and the page itself at the right with its pictures. Typing in "Search the
guide" narrows the left to the sections that hold every typed word, with the
words marked; picking one opens its page at that section. Escape empties the
search. Choosing the menu item again brings the open window to the front.
The design is on the canvas "JusPrin v2", page "JusPrin guide window", and is
a proposal Kenneth has not approved.

How it is built:
- The window is the Agent page in a new mode, ?panel=guide
  (AgentPageMode::Guide, Shell/GuideWindow), as Preferences and the import
  windows are. The page carries every docs/guide page and picture, packed in
  when it is built (guidePages.ts), so nothing is installed beside it. That
  took the page from 795 KB to 1.29 MB; WebKit on a Mac opened it in 24 ms
  instead of 22. Web/CMakeLists.txt rebuilds the page when docs/guide changes.
- The page drops what only AI reads (the ai-description line and ai: notes)
  and opens a link out of the guide in the browser only when it is https.
- Pictures are taken at twice the screen's size and shown at half, so they
  match the app. plates-tab.png was the one taken at screen size; it is
  doubled, and guide_checks.json's "atScreenSize" makes run_guide_checks.py
  double it on the next run.
- Sizes are tokens (component.guide in design-tokens.json, with a guard in
  test_brand_tokens.cpp).
- Closing the window right after opening it crashed on macOS: WebKit answered
  the page's script-handler install after the view was gone. GuideWindow
  hides and retries on a timer while an install is running, as
  Home/PopOutWindow does. The shell harness opens and closes the window to
  cover it.

Tests, on a Mac, Release build:
- AgentUI: 732 tests pass, type check passes. Guide.test.tsx checks every
  page in the index shows with every picture and none of the AI-only text,
  search, the sections list, Escape, and links.
- Shell harness: 629 checks pass, including the Help menu order, one window
  for two menu choices, and the window closing. Before the close fix the same
  run crashed with exit 139.
- brand_tokens_tests and shell_theme_tests pass. check_guide.py passes.
- In a scratch copy of the built app: Help lists the item first; the window
  opens on the print settings page with its pictures; "plate" finds three
  sections; picking one scrolls there and marks it; Escape empties the

content.text:
I committed the guide window as 2032ef71e6 on branch `claude/inspiring-aryabhata-8ac5c2`. Nothing is pushed and there is no pull request. The Help menu now starts with "JusPrin guide…". Choosing it opens a window with the guide's pages and a search box on the left, and the open page with its pictures on the right. It works in the built Mac app in light and dark.

**What it does:** You choose Help › JusPrin guide… and the window opens on the print settings page, with its sections listed under the page title. Typing "plate" narrows the left column to the three sections that contain the word, with the word marked. Clicking one scrolls the page to that section and highlights it in the list. Escape empties the search and brings the page list back. Choosing the menu item again brings the open window to the front instead of opening a second one. Text written only for the AI never shows, and a link out of the guide opens in the browser only if it is https.

**How it's built:** The window shows one more mode of the existing Agent web page, as Preferences does. The guide's pages and pictures are packed into that page when it is built. That makes the page 1.29 MB instead of 795 KB, and on this Mac it opens in 24 ms instead of 22. Packing works on every platform with nothing extra to install.

**A crash I found and fixed:** closing the window right after opening it crashed the app on the Mac. This happens when the window's web view is deleted while it is still setting up. The window now waits for that setup to finish before closing, the same way the pop-out printer window does. The shell test app crashed on that step before the fix and passes all 629 checks after it.

**Tests and results:**
- All 732 tests of the Agent web page pass, and its type check passes. The new tests cover every guide page and picture, search, Escape and links.
- The design-token and theme tests pass.
- The guide's own check for the print settings page passes. Its picture script now makes the doubled plates picture the same file I committed.
- The include check passes on every changed line.
- In a copy of the built app I checked the Help menu, opening, searching, picking a section, Escape and closing, in light and dark. I sent you five screenshots.
- A fresh reader understood the window from the screenshots. Their findings led to three small fixes: the search box no longer autocorrects "plate" to "Plate", a picked section keeps its highlight under the pointer, and a heading the window scrolls to has space above it.

**Still open:**
- Windows and Linux are untested.
- Two things on the Mac are unchecked: whether macOS adds its Search field to the top of the Help menu, and the title-bar colour when the Mac itself is in dark mode. Preferences shows the same light title bar under the per-app dark setting I used.
- Pictures stay light in the dark window, because they are light-mode screenshots.
- The window's design is a proposal Kenneth has not approved. That covers it not blocking the app, the 960 × 680 size, the page order, the search rule and packing the pictures. The boards are on the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "JusPrin guide window", and I corrected the Help-menu board to match the built app.
- The reader also tripped on the print settings page's own text, for example "Choose Plate settings…." with a doubled full stop. That page belongs to the guide work, so I didn't change it. The findings are in `guide-window-findings.md` in the shared notes folder.

**Decision needed: should the guide window stay as I built it?** The parent session described a Help window, but nobody has approved how it behaves. Here is how it behaves today:
- It doesn't block the app, so you can keep working in the project while it's open.
- It opens at 960 × 680 and lists the pages in the order the guide's README gives them.

**Decision needed: in dark mode, should the guide's pictures stay light?** Today someone in dark mode reads a dark page with light screenshots in it. They're readable, but they look pasted in. You have three options:

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

content.text:
Here's what the refactor changes. It isn't committed yet, because I'm still checking one harness failure.

**What was duplicated.** The app has five windows that hold one of our web pages: the guide, Preferences, Import from OrcaSlicer, the Add a printer conversation on Home, and the credits sheet. A printer's own pop-out window is a sixth, holding one of Orca's views. Each had its own copy of two things.

1. **Waiting before destroying a web view.** On a Mac, a window closed right after it opens can crash the app if its page is torn down too early. Four windows each had their own timer, retry loop, "closing" flag and a ten-line comment explaining the crash: the pop-out window, the credits sheet, the printer conversation and the guide.
   - Now one small class, `WebViewRelease`, does the waiting, and the explanation lives only there.
   - Each window's close is now two lines: "release now, or hide and wait".
   - The guide window lost its closing flag and its second close function. The printer conversation lost its second retry handler and its timer id. It also lost one of its two teardown paths: "destroy now" and "park it and destroy later" are now the same code.
2. **Building a throwaway document for the page.** Every page needs a chat document even when the window holds no chat. So each window made one in memory, kept it beside the view, and needed a destructor that tore things down in a careful order: clear the page's handlers, delete the view, then free the document. Getting that order wrong crashes the app.
   - Now `AgentWebView` has a second constructor that makes and owns that document itself. The ordering problem is gone.
   - Each window creates its view in one call, with no document member. Its destructor is one line, `delete m_view`, because the page's handlers call back into the window.
   - The printer panel reads its document through the view instead of keeping its own copy.

**Net size.** Removed: 230 lines. Added: 219 lines, including the new 73-line helper and its explanation. So the line count barely moves. The gain is that each of the six windows is shorter, and the crash rule now lives in one place instead of four copies that could drift apart.

**One place left as it was.** The code that swaps the whole app back to the classic Orca view still has its own timer. Its waiting step destroys the object that would own the helper, so the helper can't be used there. Its comment now points at the helper.

**Testing so far:**
- The build succeeds, and the include check passes on all 17 changed files.
- The full shell harness passes with 0 failures.
- The credits sheet's pop-up test passes.
- In a test copy of the app, I opened and closed the guide, Preferences, Import from OrcaSlicer and the Add a printer conversation. The guide closed right after opening, and choosing the menu item twice still gave one window. The app kept running throughout.

**Still checking:** the harness's printer-setup run has one failing check. After the printer conversation changes a nozzle, restoring the saved version should bring back an unsaved printer edit, and it doesn't. That's about version history, not code I touched. But the printer conversation is one of the files I changed, so I'm now building the code from before my change and running the same check, to see whether it was already failing.

input.content:
Web view windows: one helper waits out macOS before destroying a view, and the view owns its throwaway document

Six windows that hold a web view each carried their own copy of two
pieces of code. This moves both into one place each.

Waiting before a web view is destroyed. On macOS a window closed right
after it opens crashes the app if its web view goes while WebKit is
still installing the page's script handler. Home's printer pop-out,
the credits sheet, the Add a printer conversation and the guide window
each had their own retry timer, closing flag and long comment for this.
Agent/WebViewRelease now does the waiting: request() runs the release
step now, or retries every 50 ms while an install is running, and
cancel() drops it. The explanation lives there. The guide window loses
its closing flag and second close function; the printer conversation
loses its retry handler, its timer id and one of its two teardown
paths. detach_shell() keeps its own timer, because its step destroys
whatever would own the helper; its comment points at the helper.

A document for windows that hold no chat. The guide, Preferences,
Import from OrcaSlicer and the printer conversation each built an
in-memory ProjectPersistence beside their view and had to tear things
down in order: clear the page's handlers, delete the view, then free
the document. AgentWebView gains a constructor that makes and owns that
document, so the order cannot go wrong; each window creates its view in
one call and its destructor is `delete m_view`, so the page's handlers
never call into a half-destroyed window. The printer conversation reads
its document through the view.

Tests, on a Mac, Release build:
- Shell harness, default run: 0 failures.
- Harness --server-sheet-popup (the credits sheet and its pop-up): passes.
- Harness --printer-setup: its printer pop-out checks pass, including
  closing a pop-out right after opening it. That run has failures that
  are not from this change: the same checks fail, and the run crashes at
  the same point, with the code from before it.
- clang-tidy's include check passes on the changed lines.
- In a copy of the built app: the guide closed at once and reopened,
  choosing it twice gave one window; Preferences, Import from OrcaSlicer
  and the Add a printer conversation (twice) opened and closed; the app
  kept running.

Not checked: Windows and Linux; the credits sheet signed in against a
server (harness --server-sheet needs a server and a test account).

The shell harness's `--printer-setup` mode fails on `jusprin-dev`. Find the cause of each failure and fix it, with the broken behaviour reproduced before the fix and passing after.

What fails, seen 2026-11-11 on a Mac Release build (binary `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup`, run with `HOME` set to an empty scratch folder):
1. `nozzle_panel_change_keeps_the_dropped_edit_in_history` fails, in `verify_nozzle_change_leaves_the_project` in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, around line 4131. After the printer conversation's `printer_change` tool changes the nozzle, restoring the version saved before it should bring back the unsaved `printer_notes` edit, and it does not. Right after it, the run throws `filesystem error: in permissions: No such file or directory [.../jusprin/projects/<id>/pending]` (the next block sets permissions on that `pending` folder to make a save fail) and the mode ends with failures=2.
2. With that block skipped by a temporary `return;`, the run gets further. Then `home_says_not_connected_after_a_failed_host_test`, `panel_close_mid_test_closes`, `panel_reopen_does_not_read_the_old_answer` and `panel_close_mid_test_saves_nothing` fail, and the harness crashes (exit 139) after `unlinked_online_device_is_not_a_connected_saved_printer`.

The same failures and crash happen on commit 2032ef71e6 and on a later refactor of the web-view windows, so they come from earlier work. Decide for each whether the app or the test is wrong. Follow AGENTS.md: build with `-j4`, one build per build folder, and reuse the shared dependencies. Done means `--printer-setup` passes, the default harness run still passes, and the fix is committed on a branch.

The blank project behind Home was never designed or approved. OrcaSlicer's Plater holds `Slic3r::Model model` as a value member and calls `new_project` at startup (upstream `EVT_RESTORE_PROJECT` handler). JusPrin's shell keeps that Plater and gives the empty project an identity (`ProjectPersistence::attach`, `ProjectAutosave`). The "untouched startup draft" existed from 076ed1d4c3 (2026-09-30).

9d565b8e6b (2026-10-28) removed the startup reopen that used to replace the draft, so the draft became what stays open. Kenneth's words on 2026-10-28 covered only the reopen: "Let's assume this is a bug." An agent told them the removal meant "starting on Home with nothing open", and an agent brief added "a blank draft behind it".

content.text:
Six of the seven failures are fixed. I'm still working on the last one; nothing is committed yet.

**Fixed so far** (all in the uncommitted working tree):
- **The crash and five of the six Bambu connection failures** had one cause. Since OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, the app's list of nearby printers also holds LAN printers from other printer types. Here that meant the stand-in Moonraker printers that earlier checks in the same run had connected.
  - The harness took the first printer in that list as "the fake Bambu printer". It got a Moonraker entry, so connecting was refused as "a different model", and the reset call crashed on a printer that doesn't exist.
  - The harness now picks the fake printer by its id in all three places that connect it.
- **Earlier fixes**, from before this round: the nozzle check gets a model so the project has versions to compare; the Home card check reads the `no_connection` flag; closing a printer chat now ends a connection test that is still waiting.

**Still failing:** `selection_interruption_does_not_blame_credentials`. The check connects the fake printer, lets one event turn pass, then deselects it, and expects the chat to say "The selected printer changed".
- During that one event turn, upstream's Device tab handles a backlog of queued "select printer" requests: three for each stand-in Moonraker printer, then one for the fake.
- The last request disconnects and reconnects the fake. The fake answers "connection lost", and upstream's handler for "connection lost" clears the selection.
- So the chat reports a lost connection instead of a changed selection.
- A debugger run is going now to find which code queues those requests. That tells me whether this is a harness artifact or something a real person could hit.

**Something you should know:** some of my earlier runs overlapped each other and shared one scratch home folder. That caused extra timing failures, so I'm ignoring those results. The runs that matter are each one harness on its own. The machine's load also went up to 24 from other sessions, which makes the host-timeout checks flaky.

**Left to do after this:**
- Remove the temporary diagnostic prints.
- Run `--printer-setup` and the default harness.
- Run the include check.
- Delete my harness data folders.
- Commit.
Were these failures caused by your refactoring effort?

No. I checked this before changing anything, by running `--printer-setup` on two builds that don't contain the refactor:

- The main checkout's harness: the `jusprin-dev` branch, built on Nov 10, before the refactor commit existed.
- A build of this worktree from just before the refactor commit.

Both builds had the same failing checks as mine and crashed at the same point, in `MachineObject::reset`. So the failures were already there before the refactor.

The causes I've found since then also have nothing to do with web views:
- **The crash and five Bambu connection failures:** since the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge, the nearby-printer list also holds the stand-in Moonraker printers, and the harness took the first printer in the list instead of the fake Bambu one.
- **The nozzle check:** since your 2026-11-02 rule, an empty project that was never saved keeps no versions, so the check had nothing to compare.
- **The Home card check:** it compared message text that the 2026-11-06 status change replaced with the `no_connection` flag.
- **The connection-test check:** closing a printer chat didn't end a connection test that was still waiting. That was already the case before the refactor.
- **The one still failing:** a backlog of upstream Device tab selection requests clears the selection mid-connect.

The refactor only changed how windows destroy their web views, and none of these touch that.

One limit: the crash stopped those baseline runs partway through. The Bambu connection checks after the crash point never ran there, so for them I'm relying on the cause I found, not on a baseline run.

Help › JusPrin guide…: a window that searches the app guide and shows its pages

The Help menu gains "JusPrin guide…" above Ask AI…. It opens a window over
the app, not modal, 960 × 680: the guide's pages at the left in the order
docs/guide/README.md lists them, the open page's sections under its title,
and the page itself at the right with its pictures. Typing in "Search the
guide" narrows the left to the sections that hold every typed word, with the
words marked; picking one opens its page at that section. Escape empties the
search. Choosing the menu item again brings the open window to the front.
The design is on the canvas "JusPrin v2", page "JusPrin guide window", and is
a proposal Kenneth has not approved.

How it is built:
- The window is the Agent page in a new mode, ?panel=guide
  (AgentPageMode::Guide, Shell/GuideWindow), as Preferences and the import
  windows are. The page carries every docs/guide page and picture, packed in
  when it is built (guidePages.ts), so nothing is installed beside it. That
  took the page from 795 KB to 1.29 MB; WebKit on a Mac opened it in 24 ms
  instead of 22. Web/CMakeLists.txt rebuilds the page when docs/guide changes.
- The page drops what only AI reads (the ai-description line and ai: notes)
  and opens a link out of the guide in the browser only when it is https.
- Pictures are taken at twice the screen's size and shown at half, so they
  match the app. plates-tab.png was the one taken at screen size; it is
  doubled, and guide_checks.json's "atScreenSize" makes run_guide_checks.py
  double it on the next run.
- Sizes are tokens (component.guide in design-tokens.json, with a guard in
  test_brand_tokens.cpp).

Web view windows share two pieces of code that six of them each carried:

- Waiting before a web view is destroyed. On macOS a window closed right
  after it opens crashes the app if its web view goes while WebKit is still
  installing the page's script handler. The guide window hit this first.
  Agent/WebViewRelease now does the waiting: request() runs the release step
  now, or retries every 50 ms while an install is running, and cancel()
  drops it. Home's printer pop-out, the credits sheet, the Add a printer
  conversation and the guide window use it in place of their own retry
  timer, closing flag and comment. detach_shell() keeps its own timer,
  because its step destroys whatever would own the helper; its comment
  points at the helper.
- A document for windows that hold no chat. AgentWebView gains a
  constructor that makes and owns an in-memory ProjectPersistence, so the
  guide, Preferences, Import from OrcaSlicer and the printer conversation no
  longer build one beside their view and tear the two down in order. Each
  window's destructor is `delete m_view`. The printer conversation reads its
  document through the view.

Tests, on a Mac, Release build:
- AgentUI: 732 tests pass, type check passes. Guide.test.tsx checks every
  page in the index shows with every picture and none of the AI-only text,
  search, the sections list, Escape, and links.
- Shell harness, default run: 0 failures, including the Help menu order, one
  window for two menu choices, and closing the window right after opening
  it (before the wait was added, that run crashed with exit 139).
- Harness --server-sheet-popup (the credits sheet and its pop-up): passes.
- Harness --printer-setup: the printer pop-out checks pass, including
  closing a pop-out right after opening it. The run has other failures and a
  crash that are not from this change: the same checks fail, and the run
  crashes at the same point, on a build from before it.
- brand_tokens_tests and shell_theme_tests pass. check_guide.py --area
  print-settings passes, and its picture step makes plates-tab.png byte for
  byte the file committed here. clang-tidy's include check passes on the
  changed lines.
- In a copy of the built app: Help lists the item first; the window opens on
  the print settings page with its pictures; "plate" finds three sections;
  picking one scrolls there and marks it; Escape empties the search; light
  and dark both checked. The guide closed at once and reopened, choosing it
  twice gave one window; Preferences, Import from OrcaSlicer and the Add a
  printer conversation (twice) opened and closed; the app kept running.

Not checked: Windows and Linux; whether macOS adds its Search field to the
Help menu; the title bar in dark mode with the Mac itself set to dark; the
credits sheet signed in against a server.
